title: Dual differential line receiver with strobe and on-chip termination

sources.document: National Semiconductor 1975 Interface Integrated Circuits, DS7820/DS8820 dual line receiver

pins.name: IN-1
pins.text: inverting differential input (5 k input resistance typ)

pins.name: TERM1
pins.text: line termination resistor (170 ohm typ) to the non-inverting input; tie to the inverting input to use it

pins.name: STROBE1
pins.text: strobe, active low: low forces the output high; high (or open) lets the receiver work (read from the schematic, 3-22)

pins.name: RESP1
pins.text: response time control: capacitor to ground slows the receiver to reject noise spikes

functions.text: Differential line receiver: the output is high when IN+ is above IN- by more than the threshold (0 V typ, +-0.5 V max with no common mode, +-1 V over +-15 V common mode), low when below. Input range +-15 V. The output state is defined for open inputs (level not read). STROBE low forces the output high (read from the schematic on 3-22; the text states no polarity).

electrical.notes: Not a 74-style table: VOL <= 0.4 V at 3.5 mA sink, VOH 2.5..5.5 V at 0.2 mA source (fanout of two TTL). VCC 4.75..5.25 V for DS8820.

unknown: STROBE polarity is read from the transistor schematic (3-22); no sentence or truth table in the datasheet states it.
Output level for open inputs not stated in the pages read.
Output stage type: the schematic shows an emitter-follower pull-up with resistor and a transistor pull-down; recorded as totem-pole.
The ND manual calls this part "Tri-state line receiver"; the DS8820 has no three-state output. The ND pinout (1 -, 2 terminate, 3 +, 4 strobe, 6 output) matches the DS8820 exactly.
Only a typical response time is printed; no tPLH/tPHL split and no maximum.
notes: Two independent receivers. ND symbol shows one half with pin numbers of the other half in brackets.

behaviour.source: pdf 95-96 (printed 3-22, 3-23) - National 1975 Interface Integrated Circuits, DS7820/DS8820

conditions.name: DIFF1
conditions.meaning: 1 when IN+ is above IN- by more than the threshold, 0 when below (VTH 0 V typ, -0.5..+0.5 V with VIN 0, -1..+1 V over -15..+15 V common mode, 3-23). Polarity from the schematic (3-22): a higher non-inverting input turns Q2 on harder, which turns Q6, Q7, Q8 off and lets Q10 pull OUTPUT high.

outputs.source: printed 3-22, schematic: STROBE is the emitter of Q5, whose base and collector sit on the node that drives Q6 (fed by R12 from V+ and pulled down by Q2). A low STROBE pulls that node low through Q5, so Q6, Q7 and Q8 turn off and Q10 pulls OUTPUT high; with STROBE high Q5 is off (strobe current -5 uA at 5.5 V, 3-23) and the receiver works normally. The strobe current of 1.0-1.4 mA at 0.4 V (3-23) is the R12 current this path takes. Read from the schematic; the text states no polarity.
